content.content:
# Resend — transactional email for Next.js Resend sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) through a small HTTP API with delivery logs, webhooks and domain verification. The official Node.js library `resend` wraps the whole Resend REST API, has typed responses and works in Node.js 18+, serverless and edge runtimes. ## Install ```bash npm install resend ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` RESEND_API_KEY=re_placeholder RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The API key is created in the Resend dashboard (API Keys). The From address must be on a domain you have verified in Resend, or `onboarding@resend.dev` while testing. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/resend.ts`: ```ts import { Resend } from "resend"; export const resend = new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the API key to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; const { data, error } = await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Welcome!", html: "

Thanks for signing up.

", text: "Thanks for signing up.", }); ``` `data.id` is the message id; use it to look the email up in the dashboard logs. ## 4. Send with a React template Write the email as a React component and pass it with `react`; Resend renders it to HTML: ```tsx import { resend } from "@/lib/resend"; import { PasswordResetEmail } from "@/emails/password-reset"; await resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL!, to: "user@example.com", subject: "Reset your password", react: PasswordResetEmail({ name: "Ada", actionUrl: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }), }); ``` The `@react-email/components` package gives layout primitives for email clients; plain JSX works too. ## 5. Handle errors `emails.send` does not throw on a refused message: it resolves to `{ data: null, error }` with the error `name` and `message` from Resend (invalid API key, unverified domain, rate limit). Check `error` where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Resend - Built for developers: one API call to send, typed SDK, React templates in the codebase. - Delivery logs, bounces and webhooks live in the same dashboard as the API keys. - Domain verification with DKIM and SPF guided from the dashboard. # env files (can opt-in for committing if needed) .env* next-env.d.ts @alloc @babel @emnapi

content.text:
I added Resend email to Notely. New users now get a welcome email and there's a working password-reset email flow, both wired into `src/lib/users.ts`. `next build` and lint pass. I haven't sent a real email, because that needs a real API key and a verified sending domain.

**Why Resend:** it's built for transactional email in Next.js apps, the Node library is small and typed, and the logs, bounces and domain setup are all in one dashboard. I used the official `resend` package (v6).

**Changes in `src/lib/users.ts`:**
- **`createUser({ email, name })`**: rejects an email that's already registered, adds the user, then sends the welcome email.
- **`requestPasswordReset(email)`**: creates a random reset token that expires in 60 minutes and emails a link to `/reset-password?token=…`. Only a hash of the token is stored, and a new request cancels any earlier links. If the email isn't registered it returns the same way and sends nothing, so it can't be used to check which addresses have accounts.
- **`consumePasswordResetToken(token)`**: checks the token, makes sure it can only be used once, and returns the user it belongs to.
- **`getUserByEmail(email)`**: new lookup helper.

**Supporting files:**
- **`src/lib/resend.ts`**: the Resend client is created on first send, so a missing key only causes an error when an email goes out, not when the app loads.
- **`src/lib/email.ts`**: `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`. If an email fails to send, the error is logged and returned rather than thrown, so a failed email never breaks sign-up or reset.
- **`src/emails/`**: the two templates, as HTML with a plain-text version and user input escaped. I wrote them as plain strings rather than React templates, which avoids adding another rendering dependency.
- **`.env.example`**: placeholders for `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` and `APP_URL`. `.gitignore` was ignoring every `.env*` file, including this one, so I added an exception for `.env.example`.
- I also added the `server-only` package, so the email code fails the build if it's ever imported into browser code.

**Still missing:**
- **No pages call these functions yet.** There's no sign-up form, no "forgot password" form, and no `/reset-password` page to land on from the email link.
- **No password storage.** `User` has no password field, so `consumePasswordResetToken` only identifies the user; actually saving a new password has to be added when real auth exists.
- **Users and reset tokens are kept in memory**, like the existing users list, so they're lost when the server restarts.
- **To go live:** create a key in the Resend dashboard, verify your sending domain (or use `onboarding@resend.dev` while testing), and put the values in `.env.local`.

`tsc --noEmit` on its own reports an error in `src/app/layout.tsx`, which I didn't touch. It's a type that Next generates during a build; `next build` passes.

Nothing is committed.
